text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 fired: LB target-health degraded (us-west-2). Auto-escalation enabled.

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident #INC-199850 — P1 — Severity: customer-impacting — Acknowledgment required by oncall-sre.

oncall-sre: acked. I'm on it. seeing spike in 5xx + TLS handshake failures from edge. tagging network-eng and infra. :eyes:

Evelyn: I can look at ALB config, pulling target group health now. any recent deploys?

Samir: I didn't push infra changes. My last deploy was 03:40 UTC. Checking recent routing changes and cert rotations.

oncall-sre: metrics -> increased 525/526-style TLS failures (handshake/timeouts) to upstream targets. Latency also up 200ms. Customers report chat/generation timeouts.

support-team: multiple customer tickets since 07:11 UTC, many from EU -> maybe routing shifted to us-west.

oncall-sre: quick checks:
```
# ALB target health
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:... | jq '.TargetHealthDescriptions[] | {Id: .Target.Id, State: .TargetHealth.State, Reason: .TargetHealth.Reason}'
# sample output
# {"Id":"i-0abc...","State":"unhealthy","Reason":"TLS handshake failed"}
```

oncall-sre: curl to one of backend instances returns TLS handshake abort: `curl: (35) SSL connect error`. Packet drops observed on port 443.

Natalie: DNS check: the fronting ALB endpoint is resolving to multiple AZ IPs. TTL is 300s. No recent Route53 changes in last 24h according to audit log.

Mike: running dig +trace -> some resolvers still returning old IPs for the failover ALB. Could be slow propagation after yesterday's maintenance.

Evelyn: I see a Canary ALB routing rule added yesterday by a routing tweak — it pointed small percent to a new target group in us-west-2 which now has unhealthy nodes. Rolling that change back now.

oncall-sre: action 1: remove canary routing from ALB (rollback). action 2: drain unhealthy targets in us-west-2 and shift traffic to us-east-1 fallbacks. action 3: increase tracing, set alert thresholds to avoid flapping.

Evelyn: rollback applied. Confirming new routing state.

Samir: executing failover plan:
```
# move 100% traffic to us-east fallback
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn ... --default-actions '[{"Type":"forward","TargetGroupArn":"arn:aws:...:us-east-1:tg/primary"}]'
# drain targets
kubectl scale deployment inference-backend -n prod --replicas=0 --context=us-west-2
```

oncall-sre: after failover, 60% reduction in TLS errors in 90s, 90% reduction at 6m. Latency normalizing. :tada:

support-team: customers still seeing intermittent errors from EU mobile networks — likely DNS caches. We're sending a support blurb with expected recovery timeline and mitigation steps.

Natalie: DNS TTL is 300 so some resolvers will keep using the failed IPs until expiration. We can open a communication to ISPs but that's not reliable. Suggest we keep failover active for 1 hour then re-evaluate.

Mike: noticed certificate handshake errors on a subset of backends — looks like an automated cert rotation job failed to update certs on the canary group. That's the root cause for the target health failures.

Samir: confirming: cert-rotator job failed due to permission error when writing to the instance. I'll patch the cert-rotator and re-run on a test target group.

Evelyn: for immediate safety, keep us-west-2 targets out of rotation until certs validated.

oncall-sre: escalation summary for on-call lead:
- Impact: 30-40% error rate for API calls routed to us-west-2, customer-facing timeouts and TLS errors. Some EU users affected due to resolver selection.
- Mitigation: Rolled back canary, failed over to us-east-1 fallback, drained and quarantined unhealthy targets.
- Current status: Traffic routed to fallback; metrics stable and errors declining. DNS propagation may cause residual client errors for up to TTL window (~5 minutes to 5 minutes*1? - actually TTL 300s).

pagerduty: auto-escalation suppressed (ack received). If errors climb back above threshold, page will re-fire.

Samir: follow-ups: patch cert rotator (root cause), run cert refresh on quarantined instances, add RBAC fix to CI, add canary rollout guardrail to prevent routing 100% to canary accidentally.

Evelyn: I'll open a post-incident PR to relax the canary weight UI and add validation to the operator.

support-team: we've sent status update to effected customers: ETA for full recovery 30-60 minutes pending DNS TTL. No major data loss reported.

oncall-sre: handing off to Mike (next-oncall) for monitoring and root-cause follow-up. Handoff notes:
- Keep failover active until certs validated and target group health green in us-west-2 for at least 30m.
- Confirm all certs present and valid on backend instances.
- Re-run small canary (5%) after validation with strict health-check thresholds.

Mike: taking over. I'll watch metrics for the next 2 hours and coordinate the cert rotation. :thumbsup:

Evelyn: tagging owners: network-eng for ALB routing guardrails, infra for cert-rotator patch, oncall-sre for postmortem.

Samir: created follow-up issues: INFRA-654 (cert-rotator RBAC fix), NET-321 (canary routing validation), PM-qa for post-incident checks.

oncall-sre: postmortem required. Please include timeline, root cause (cert rotation failure + canary routing), impact assessment, customer communication, and remediation steps.

support-team: will compile customer impact summary and attach ticket IDs to the incident doc.

incident-bot: Incident #INC-199850 acknowledged and assigned. Status: mitigated -> monitoring.

Mike: final note before close: if errors resurge, re-escalate immediately. Otherwise we will transition to a formal incident review tomorrow.

support-team: closing channel for proactive updates, we'll reopen if anything changes. :white_check_mark:
